reqs.text: The system shall let an officer look up a farmer by NIN through NIMC before enrolment.
reqs.uml: UC diagram (Fig. 4.1) UC-01; SD-1 Issuance sequence (Fig. 4.2)

reqs.text: The system shall capture the farmer's photo and embed it as a small signed thumbnail.
The system shall sign a credential holding its ID, masked NIN, name, ward, LGA, state, validity dates, key ID, level and (L2) holder key.
reqs.uml: SD-1 Issuance sequence (Fig. 4.2); SM-2 Credential lifecycle (Fig. 3.2)

reqs.text: For L2, the wallet shall generate a device key and the system shall bind its public key into the credential.
reqs.uml: SD-1 Issuance sequence (Fig. 4.2); SM-2 Credential lifecycle (Fig. 3.2) PendingBinding

reqs.text: For L1, the system shall produce a printable paper wallet carrying the signed QR.
reqs.uml: UC diagram (Fig. 4.1) UC-04; SM-2 Credential lifecycle (Fig. 3.2)

reqs.text: The system shall allow at most one active credential per NIN, revoking the old one atomically on re-issue (D8).
reqs.uml: SD-1 Issuance sequence (Fig. 4.2) opt re-issue; Class diagram (Fig. 3.3) rule 2

reqs.text: The system shall let an officer revoke a credential with a recorded reason.
reqs.uml: SD-3 Revocation & sync sequence (Fig. 4.4); SM-2 Credential lifecycle (Fig. 3.2) Revoked

reqs.text: The Trust service shall publish the issuer public keys with their key IDs.
The system shall publish a signed, versioned revocation list, and the Trust service shall verify it and refuse rollback (D11).
reqs.uml: SD-3 Revocation & sync sequence (Fig. 4.4); Class diagram (Fig. 3.3) RevocationList

reqs.text: The wallet shall hold several farmer profiles on one shared phone, each with its own key and PIN.
The wallet shall show a credential only after the profile PIN is entered.
The wallet shall sign the challenge and credential ID with the device key and show the answer as a QR.
The wallet shall perform all its functions with no network after enrolment.
reqs.code: web Wallet.tsx (no API calls); PWA service worker

reqs.text: The verifier shall let an agent sign in online once and then work offline for 7 days. (Agent PIN unlock not built: the 7-day token is kept on the phone.)
The verifier shall download the keys and revocation list when online and on demand, and check the list signature itself.
The verifier shall check the issuer signature offline.
reqs.uml: SD-2 Offline verification sequence (Fig. 4.3); SM-1 Verification state machine (Fig. 3.1) CredentialRead

reqs.text: For L2, the verifier shall issue a fresh random challenge and verify the wallet's answer against the holder key.
reqs.uml: SD-2 Offline verification sequence (Fig. 4.3); SM-1 Verification state machine (Fig. 3.1) ChallengeShown

reqs.text: The verifier shall check expiry and revocation against its cached list.
The verifier shall show the signed photo or details and require the agent to confirm the face before acceptance.
The verifier shall show the verdict as Accepted (L2), Accepted (L1) or Rejected with a reason.
The verifier shall warn when its list is older than 7 days and refuse acceptances when it is older than 30 days.
The verifier shall record every attempt, accepted or rejected, in a local queue.
The system shall not support proxy or delegated presentation; the holder must be present (D6).
The system shall upload queued records in batches and append them to a signed hash chain, taking the agent's identity from the token.
The system shall let an auditor filter records and run a chain-integrity check.
The system shall flag a credential accepted at two different points within 24 hours (possible cloning).
The system shall authenticate staff by username and password. (TOTP MFA for Admin/Auditor deferred: cut list item 2.)
reqs.uml: UC diagram (Fig. 4.1) UC-11; SD-1 Issuance sequence (Fig. 4.2)

reqs.text: The system shall enforce role-based access (Officer, Agent, Admin, Auditor) on every endpoint.
The system shall let an administrator create, disable and unlock staff accounts and assign agents to distribution points.
Offline verification (scan to verdict, excluding people) within 3 s on a low-end phone.
Credential issuance completes within 5 s.
Core verification available with zero connectivity; services degrade gracefully when one is down.
Ed25519 signing; issuer private key only in the Issuer, encrypted at rest (HSM in production).
Holder private keys sealed with a PIN-derived key (PBKDF2 + AES-GCM).
TLS on all traffic. (Prototype: HTTPS between phones and the app; services on localhost behind the proxy. Production: TLS reverse proxy.)
Data minimisation: masked NIN only; full NIN never stored (keyed hash, D13).
Fail securely: any error, unknown key or bad input is a rejection, never a crash or leak.
Audit records tamper-evident: hash chain with each record hash signed by the Audit service.
Login rate-limited; account locks after 5 failed logins.
Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 principles. (Minimisation and purpose limitation built in; consent capture is a procedural step at enrolment.)
Hausa and English. (Verdict strings in Hausa; full translation deferred.)
Verdicts readable without reading English: colour, icon, Hausa word.
An L2 verification takes at most 4 agent taps.
Usable on 5-inch screens; touch targets at least 48 px.
Credential QR at most 1,800 bytes, including a photo thumbnail.
Wallet stores up to 5 profiles in at most 5 MB.
Revocation list of 100,000 entries transferred and cached in at most 2 MB (compressed). First test failed at 2.40 MB uncompressed; fixed with gzip in transit and deflate in the phone cache.
At least 2,000 queued records per upload.
